headings.title: Mandatory interdepartmental information exchange rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires the departments of health and senior services and social services to promulgate rules and regulations for exchanging information, including regulatory violations, to protect individuals served by regulated health care providers.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Conditions effectiveness of rules promulgated under this section on compliance with chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 191.005 requiring interdepartmental information exchange rules between health and senior services and social services and compliance with chapter 536.

headings.title: Prohibition on premises for illicit self-administration
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits knowingly operating or controlling premises to allow individuals to self-administer preobtained controlled substances not authorized by chapters 195 and 579.

headings.title: Exemptions for licensed health care facilities
headings.reviewNote: Exempts licensed chapter 197 or 198 health care facilities providing medical assistance, monitoring, sterile supplies, or syringe disposal services.

headings.title: Preservation of overdose medical assistance immunity
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section does not affect statutory immunity under section 195.205 for reporting or experiencing a drug overdose.

headings.title: Definition of controlled substance
headings.reviewNote: Defines controlled substance as a drug, substance, or immediate precursor in Schedules I through V listed in chapter 195.

headings.title: Authority and criteria to designate eligible facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to designate eligible facilities in areas of need based on population health, ability to pay, accessibility, and provider availability.

headings.title: Six-year designation reevaluation and burden of proof
headings.reviewNote: Requires department reevaluation every six years and places the burden of proof on the facility to show ongoing qualification.

headings.title: Revocation restrictions and opportunity for input
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits revoking designation before affording interested area persons opportunity to submit supporting data and information.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative rulemaking subject to chapter 536 procedures and specifies nonseverability clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 191.1053 governing eligible facility designation in areas of defined need, sexennial reevaluations, revocation procedures, and rulemaking nonseverability.

headings.title: Creation, custody, and authorized disbursements of fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Health Care Access Fund in the state treasury and authorizes appropriated disbursements to eligible facilities for recruitment, facilities, equipment, and primary care costs.

headings.title: State general revenue matching schedule
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state to provide one-half matching moneys up to statutory annual caps of $500,000 for FY 2008, $1.5 million for FY 2009, and $1 million annually thereafter.

headings.title: Donation limits, tax credits, and equipment eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Caps annual donations per individual or corporation at $50,000, grants a 50% tax credit under section 135.575 (noted in source as repealed in 2018) for contributions of $100 or more excluding nonprofit corporations, and includes donated equipment without state matching funds.

headings.title: Recapture of moneys upon facility closure or reduction
headings.reviewNote: Requires refunding fund disbursements and the general revenue match to each appropriate source if a clinic or facility closes or significantly decreases operations within one year of receiving moneys.

headings.title: Exemption from state fund lapse provisions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts fund balances from section 33.080 biennial transfer to general revenue, ensuring unexpended balances remain in the fund.

headings.title: Investment and crediting of fund interest
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state treasurer to invest fund moneys and credit all earned interest to the Missouri Health Care Access Fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 191.1056 establishing the Missouri Health Care Access Fund, state matching appropriations, donation limits and tax credits, recapture upon closure, nonreversion, and investment of fund moneys.

headings.title: Creation and purpose of palliative care council
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Palliative Care and Quality of Life Interdisciplinary Council within the department of health and senior services.

headings.title: Appointment and composition of council members
headings.reviewNote: Requires appointment on or before December 1, 2016, of four legislators, two hospice and palliative physicians, two nurses, a social worker, a patient and family caregiver advocate, and a spiritual professional.

headings.title: Terms of office, officers, and meetings
headings.reviewNote: Establishes three-year member terms, election of chair and vice chair, and meeting frequency of at least twice per year.

headings.title: Compensation and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that council members serve without compensation but shall, subject to appropriations, be reimbursed for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Advisory duties and palliative care assessments
headings.reviewNote: Directs the council to consult with and advise the department on establishing, maintaining, operating, and evaluating palliative care initiatives, including the program under section 191.1085.

headings.title: Annual report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual report to the general assembly assessing palliative care availability for patients at early stages of serious disease and analyzing barriers to greater access.

headings.title: Statutory expiration of council
headings.reviewNote: Sets automatic expiration of the council on August 28, 2022.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 191.1080 creating the Missouri Palliative Care and Quality of Life Interdisciplinary Council, council membership, terms, expenses, advisory duties, annual reporting, and expiration date.

headings.title: Establishment of information and education program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Palliative Care Consumer and Professional Information and Education Program within the department.

headings.title: Program purpose for palliative care information
headings.reviewNote: Defines program purpose to maximize palliative care effectiveness by ensuring comprehensive and accurate information and education for the public, health care providers, and health care facilities.

headings.title: Publication of website information and links
headings.reviewNote: Requires publishing website resources and external links on provider continuing education, palliative care delivery across care settings, and consumer educational and referral materials including hospice.

headings.title: Encouragement of hospital website presence
headings.reviewNote: Encourages each hospital to maintain an intranet or internet presence providing palliative care education and resources.

headings.title: Encouragement of hospital patient education materials
headings.reviewNote: Encourages each hospital in the state to make patient education information about palliative care available for distribution to patients.

headings.title: Mandatory consultation with advisory council
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to consult with the palliative care and quality of life council in developing and administering the program.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative rules subject to chapter 536 procedures and specifies nonseverability clause.

headings.title: Automatic expiration date notwithstanding sunset act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that, notwithstanding section 23.253, the program authorized under this section automatically expires on August 28, 2022.

headings.title: Short title of Volunteer Health Services Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 191.1100 to 191.1112 as the Volunteer Health Services Act.

headings.title: Definitions for volunteer health services act
headings.reviewNote: Defines gross deviation, health care provider, licensed health care provider, regularly practice, sponsoring organization, and voluntary provision of health care services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 191.1100 establishing the Volunteer Health Services Act and defining statutory terms.

headings.title: Exemption from additional state licensure for volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts voluntary health care services from additional Missouri licensure or certification for a licensed health care provider or person lawfully practicing under a licensure exception of any U.S. jurisdiction who does not regularly practice in Missouri.

headings.title: Exclusions from volunteer licensure exemption
headings.reviewNote: Excludes persons whose license or certificate is suspended or revoked under disciplinary proceedings in any jurisdiction and providers rendering services outside their authorized scope of practice.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 191.1102 exempting volunteer health care providers from additional state licensure or certification and establishing eligibility exclusions.

headings.title: Mandatory sponsoring organization registration and filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires sponsoring organizations to register annually with the department, pay a $50 annual registration fee, file required organizational details, and report changes in writing within 30 days.

headings.title: Quarterly voluntary services report and retention
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly reports listing volunteer providers and mandates maintaining service records on file for five years.

headings.title: Maintenance of volunteer provider license verification
headings.reviewNote: Requires organizations to maintain copies of licenses, certifications, exemption statements, or state website verifications for all volunteer providers.

headings.title: Five-year recordkeeping and regulatory inspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires five-year record retention and production upon request to any state healing arts regulatory board.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of due care in selection
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that compliance with registration and reporting is prima facie evidence of due care in selecting volunteer providers.

headings.title: Revocation of sponsoring organization registration
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to revoke the registration of any sponsoring organization failing to comply with section requirements.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Conditions effectiveness of rules created under this section on chapter 536 compliance and sets nonseverability invalidating rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2013, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Non-mandated participation in liability protection program
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that free care providers or organizations are not required to register or claim liability protection under the act.

headings.title: Civil immunity and conditions for volunteer providers
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from civil damages absent gross deviation or willful misconduct, conditioned on lack of compensation, scope of practice, and clinic authorization.

headings.title: Deemed licensure for active-duty military personnel
headings.reviewNote: Deems active-duty commissioned or contract medical officers and dentists assigned to federal military hospitals or medical facilities to be licensed for purposes of this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 191.1110 granting civil immunity for volunteer health care providers and deeming active-duty military medical personnel licensed.

headings.title: Definitions for volunteer crisis response teams
headings.reviewNote: Defines crisis intervention, crisis response services, critical incident stress management team member, registered team, training session, and volunteer.

headings.title: Tort and civil liability immunity for team members
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from tort liability and civil damages for registered volunteer team members acting within accepted protocols absent gross deviation or willful misconduct.

headings.title: Exclusions from crisis response tort immunity
headings.reviewNote: Excludes tort immunity for actual malice or willful intent to injure, acts outside assigned duties or without team dispatch, crimes, sexual harassment or sexual/physical abuse, moral turpitude or misconduct, or gross deviation or willful misconduct.

headings.title: Establishment and management of Show-Me ECHO Program
headings.reviewNote: Directs the University of Missouri, subject to appropriations, to manage the Show-Me ECHO Program in collaboration with the department of health and senior services.

headings.title: Program purpose and telehealth technology utilization
headings.reviewNote: Defines program design to use telehealth technology to train primary care providers and expand chronic disease treatment capacity in underserved areas.

headings.title: Utilization of local community health care workers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the program to utilize local community health care workers with knowledge of local social determinants as a force multiplier for better patient compliance and health outcomes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 191.1140 establishing the Show-Me Extension for Community Health Care Outcomes (ECHO) Program, telehealth design and purpose, and mandatory use of local community health care workers.

headings.title: Definitions for telehealth services
headings.reviewNote: Defines asynchronous store-and-forward transfer, clinical staff, distant site, health care provider, originating site, and telehealth or telemedicine.

headings.title: Authorization and standard of care for telehealth
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed health care providers to deliver telehealth within their scope of practice under the same standard of care as in-person services.

headings.title: Mandatory Missouri licensure for treating state patients
headings.reviewNote: Requires providers treating patients in Missouri via telehealth to be fully licensed in Missouri and regulated by their professional licensing boards.

headings.title: Exceptions to in-state licensure requirement
headings.reviewNote: Exempts informal uncompensated out-of-state consultations, emergency or disaster assistance without charge, and episodic physician consultations.

headings.title: Preservation of scope of practice and authorized settings
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that telehealth authorization does not alter provider scope of practice or authorize care delivery in unauthorized settings.

headings.title: Originating site clinical staffing and platform flexibility
headings.reviewNote: Provides that originating sites need not maintain immediate on-site clinical staff except when necessary to meet the standard of care, and protects electronic platform choice.

headings.title: Preservation of collaborative practice requirements
headings.reviewNote: Affirms that telehealth provisions do not alter collaborative practice requirements under chapters 334 and 335.

headings.title: Physician-patient relationship required for telehealth
headings.reviewNote: Requires an established physician-patient relationship prior to telehealth services, outlining establishment methods including in-person exam, cross-coverage, or technology.

headings.title: Prior clinical evaluation and examination requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires sufficient technology for informed diagnosis, prior patient evaluation, medical history review, and examination, sets standards for internet or telephone questionnaires, and requires providers using questionnaires to be employed by or contracted with a licensed Missouri health care business entity.

headings.title: Fourteen-day report to primary health care provider
headings.reviewNote: Requires a provider using an internet or telephone evaluation questionnaire to send a written report within 14 days to the patient's primary health care provider, if provided, detailing patient identity, evaluation date, diagnosis and treatment, and further instructions.

headings.title: Short title of CARE Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates section 191.1150 as the Caregiver, Advise, Record, and Enable (CARE) Act.

headings.title: Definitions for CARE Act
headings.reviewNote: Defines admission, after-care, ambulatory surgical center, caregiver, discharge, hospital, and residence (with excluded facilities).

headings.title: Opportunity to designate caregiver and written consent
headings.reviewNote: Requires hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers to offer an opportunity to designate a caregiver with written consent to release needed medical records, permits changing caregivers prior to discharge, and states designation creates no obligation.

headings.title: Documentation of caregiver designation and contact details
headings.reviewNote: Requires the hospital or ambulatory surgical center to document the caregiver designation, relationship to the patient, and available contact information.

headings.title: Documentation of patient declination to designate caregiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires the hospital or ambulatory surgical center to document if the patient or legal guardian declines to designate a caregiver.

headings.title: Caregiver notification of discharge or transfer
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the caregiver of discharge or transfer as soon as practicable, states inability to contact shall not delay care or discharge, and mandates documenting contact attempts.

headings.title: Provision of discharge plan and after-care instructions
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing a contacted and willing caregiver prior to discharge with the patient's discharge plan or after-care instructions and an opportunity to ask questions.

headings.title: No duty to assess caregiver ability to perform tasks
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a hospital or ambulatory surgical center is not required or obligated to determine a caregiver's ability to understand or perform after-care tasks.

headings.title: No caregiver compensation by state or health carriers
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section authorizes or requires caregiver compensation by a state agency or section 376.1350 health carrier.

headings.title: Nonduplication with federal Medicare and accrediting rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers are not required to take actions inconsistent with or duplicative of federal Medicare Title XVIII or national accrediting organization standards.

headings.title: Prohibition on private right of action against facilities
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section creates a private right of action against a hospital, ambulatory surgical center, employee, or contractor.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for caregiver acts or omissions
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, employees, and contractors from any liability for an act or omission of the caregiver.

headings.title: Protection from adverse licensing actions or sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no act or omission under this section by a hospital, ambulatory surgical center, employee, or contractor shall give rise to a citation, sanction, or other adverse licensing action.

headings.title: Noninterference with durable power of health care
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in this section interferes with the rights of an attorney-in-fact under a durable power of health care in sections 404.800 to 404.872.

headings.title: Department standard form and CMS-compliant facility forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of health and senior services to provide a standard form and permits continued use of CMS-compliant facility communication or disclosure forms.

headings.title: Establishment and membership of Alzheimer's task force
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the 21-member Alzheimer's State Plan Task Force in the department of health and senior services and specifies all member roles.

headings.title: Gubernatorial appointment and uncompensated service
headings.reviewNote: Provides for gubernatorial appointment with senate advice and consent for non-ex-officio members and specifies service without compensation.

headings.title: Task force assessment duties and plan updates
headings.reviewNote: Charges task force with assessing disease trends, evaluating care services, and updating the state Alzheimer's plan.

headings.title: Initial report of recommendations by January 1, 2023
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to deliver a report of recommendations to the governor and general assembly no later than January 1, 2023.

headings.title: Annual follow-up meetings and supplemental report updates
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to meet at the chair's request at least annually to evaluate implementation and impact and submit annual supplemental report updates to the governor and general assembly.

headings.title: Statutory expiration of Alzheimer's task force
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the provisions of this section expire on December 31, 2027.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 191.116 establishing the 21-member Alzheimer's State Plan Task Force, appointments and uncompensated service, assessment duties, January 1, 2023 report deadline, annual supplemental updates, and December 31, 2027 expiration.

headings.title: Short title of Substance Use Disorders Care Access Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 191.1164 to 191.1168 as the Ensuring Access to High Quality Care for the Treatment of Substance Use Disorders Act.

headings.title: Definitions for substance use disorder treatment access
headings.reviewNote: Defines 14 terms including behavioral therapy, department of insurance, financial requirements, health care professional, health insurance plan, health insurer, MHPAEA, NQTL, pharmacologic therapy, pharmacy benefits manager, prior authorization, QTL, step therapy, and urgent health care service.

headings.title: Inclusion of substance use care as urgent service
headings.reviewNote: Provides that urgent health care service includes services provided for the treatment of substance use disorders.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 191.1164 enacting the Ensuring Access to High Quality Care for the Treatment of Substance Use Disorders Act, defining 14 terms, and including substance use disorder treatment as an urgent health care service.

headings.title: Formulary inclusion of approved MAT medications
headings.reviewNote: Requires health insurer or pharmacy benefits manager formularies, or opioid treatment program medical benefit coverage, to include buprenorphine, methadone, naloxone, naltrexone (including extended-release injectable), and buprenorphine/naloxone combination.

headings.title: Lowest cost-sharing formulary tier placement for MAT
headings.reviewNote: Requires all MAT medications required under this section to be placed on the lowest cost-sharing tier of the insurer or pharmacy benefits manager formulary.

headings.title: Prohibited dollar, parity, step therapy, and prior-auth limits
headings.reviewNote: Bars annual or lifetime dollar limits, non-MHPAEA financial or quantitative limits, conflicting step therapy, and prior authorization for required MAT medications.

headings.title: Applicability to all Missouri health insurance plans
headings.reviewNote: Applies the MAT medication requirements of this section to all health insurance plans delivered in Missouri.

headings.title: Treatment program disclosure of MAT services and levels
headings.reviewNote: Requires entities holding themselves out as or applying for licensure as substance use treatment programs to disclose MAT services provided and independently certified levels of care.

headings.title: MO HealthNet coverage and preferred drug list inclusion
headings.reviewNote: Requires MO HealthNet to cover required MAT medications and services and include all current and new FDA-approved substance use disorder medications on its preferred drug lists.

headings.title: Correctional assessment and MAT access for inmates
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of corrections and state entities caring for detained or incarcerated persons, subject to appropriations, to assess persons for substance abuse disorders and provide physician-planned MAT without arbitrary limits on medication, dose, or duration.

headings.title: Drug court and diversion assessment and MAT access
headings.reviewNote: Requires drug courts and diversion programs to ensure physician diagnostic assessment for substance use disorders and provide physician-planned MAT without limits on medication, dose, or duration.

headings.title: Coverage eligibility regardless of prior treatment history
headings.reviewNote: Provides that MAT coverage requirements shall not depend on a patient's prior treatment success or relapse history.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of sickle cell committee
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Sickle Cell Standing Committee in the department and details required member qualifications.

headings.title: Appointment of members and uncompensated service

headings.title: Required focus areas of assessment and recommendations

headings.reviewNote: Directs the committee to meet at least annually after 2027 and submit annual supplemental findings reports.

headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director of social services to lease departmental land previously used for grazing or farming determined to be excess.

headings.title: Sealed bidding procedures through division of purchasing
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state director of purchasing to offer leases through sealed public bids with right to reject all bids.

headings.title: Lease term, renewal options, and tenant maintenance duties
headings.reviewNote: Caps lease terms at one year with annual renewal options and requires lessees to maintain land, fences, and buildings.

headings.reviewNote: Directs administrative facility officials to conduct periodic property inspections to ensure lease covenant compliance.

headings.title: Short title of visitation acts
headings.reviewNote: Designates section as the Compassionate Care Visitation Act and No Patient Left Alone Act.

headings.title: Definitions for compassionate care visitation
headings.reviewNote: Defines compassionate care visitor, compassionate care visit circumstances, and health care facility.

headings.title: Mandatory visitation hours and visitor allowance
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to allow at least two simultaneous visitors during visiting hours of at least six hours daily including evenings, weekends, and holidays, while permitting additional restrictions on children under age 14.

headings.title: Minimum standards for facility visitation policy
headings.reviewNote: Mandates policies allowing 24-hour attendance when appropriate, flexible entry and exit, and minor child parental presence.

headings.title: Preservation of communication aids and ADA compliance
headings.reviewNote: Affirms facility duties to provide communication accommodations and comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

headings.title: Permitted limitations and safety restrictions on visitors
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reasonable limits on visitor counts, restricted areas, patient requests, court orders, clinical harm, or infectious symptoms.

headings.title: Shared-room visitor redirection and safety restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Preserves facility authority to limit or redirect visitors in shared rooms for patient health and safety and to adopt reasonable safety, security, or other visitor requirements.

headings.title: Preservation of long-term care facility residents' rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not waive or change long-term care facility residents' rights under sections 198.088 and 198.090.

headings.title: Informational materials on visitation rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department by January 1, 2023, to develop informational materials and requires facilities to make them accessible upon admission or registration and on their primary website.

headings.title: Department complaint process for visitation violations
headings.reviewNote: Permits compassionate care visitors to report violations to the department and requires investigation within 36 hours in compliance with hospital, hospice, and long-term care complaint statutes.

headings.title: Civil liability immunity for participating facilities
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes health care facilities from damages in liability claims arising from compliance with this section, excluding recklessness or willful misconduct and without limiting other immunities.

headings.title: Nonwaiver except during chapter 44 declared emergency
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall not be terminated, suspended, or waived except by a chapter 44 emergency declaration, during which sections 191.2290 and 630.202 apply.

headings.title: Authorization to open long-term dignity savings account
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individuals beginning January 1, 2021, to open long-term dignity savings accounts (including multiple or joint married-filing-combined accounts) and requires compliance for the section 143.1160 tax deduction.

headings.title: Designation and qualification of account beneficiary
headings.reviewNote: Requires designating a qualified beneficiary by April 15 of the following year, allows self-designation and changes, limits each account to one beneficiary and one account per holder-beneficiary pair, while allowing one person to be beneficiary of multiple accounts.

headings.title: Unlimited retention duration without recapture or penalty
headings.reviewNote: Permits moneys to remain in a long-term dignity savings account for an unlimited duration without interest or income being subject to recapture or penalty.

headings.title: Bar on administration fees and documentation duty
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using account moneys to pay administration expenses except financial institution service fees, and makes the account holder responsible for maintaining account and eligible-expense documentation.

headings.title: Permitted tax-advantaged uses of account moneys
headings.reviewNote: Permits account moneys to be used for a qualified beneficiary's eligible expenses, transferred to another newly created dignity savings account, or used to pay a financial institution service fee.

headings.title: Tax recapture for early or nonqualified withdrawals
headings.reviewNote: Subjects withdrawals to Missouri adjusted gross income recapture if made less than one year after first deposit or used for any purpose other than those permitted in subsection 1.

headings.title: Five and ten percent penalties and death exception
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a 5% penalty on recaptured withdrawals within 10 years of first deposit and a 10% penalty after 10 years, with an exception if the qualified beneficiary died and no new beneficiary is designated that tax year.

headings.title: Disposition of remaining funds upon death of holder
headings.reviewNote: Subjects tax-deducted account moneys to recapture without penalty upon the death of the account holder or joint holders if there is no surviving transfer-on-death beneficiary.

headings.reviewNote: Provides that no financial institution shall be required to designate accounts or beneficiaries in its systems, track withdrawn moneys, or report information not otherwise required by law.

headings.title: No financial institution liability for tax or expense uses
headings.reviewNote: Relieves financial institutions of responsibility or liability for determining section 143.1160 deduction eligibility, ensuring eligible expense use, or reporting or remitting related taxes or penalties.

headings.title: Ban on nonstandard departmental requirements on institutions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department from establishing administrative, reporting, or other requirements on financial institutions outside normal account procedures.

headings.title: Short title of Missouri Save Adolescents from Experimentation Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates section 191.1720 as the Missouri Save Adolescents from Experimentation (SAFE) Act.

headings.title: Definitions for adolescent gender transition restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Defines biological sex, cross-sex hormones, gender, gender transition, gender transition surgery, health care provider, and puberty-blocking drugs.

headings.title: Prohibition on minor gender transition surgeries
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits health care providers from performing gender transition surgeries on any individual under eighteen years of age.

headings.title: Annual fee adjustment based on consumer price index

headings.title: Written patient notification of caregiver program

headings.title: Department guidelines and facility visitation standards
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop standards allowing two caregivers, at least four hours daily access, physical contact, and safety rules.

headings.title: Facility suspension requests and state defense of access
headings.reviewNote: Governs facility requests to suspend visitation for up to seven days, department oversight, and attorney general legal defense of state access.

headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that essential caregivers are not required to provide necessary care and facilities cannot mandate care provision.

headings.reviewNote: Requires health carriers to reimburse for mercury-free or lower-mercury vaccines at rates equivalent to other approved vaccines.

headings.title: Public health emergency exemption by director and governor
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department director, with gubernatorial concurrence, to exempt a vaccine upon finding an actual or potential public health emergency or supply shortage affecting pregnant women or children under age three, and to set its duration.

headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the patient of any examination performed under subdivisions (2) to (4) of subsection 2 (diagnostic/treatment, forensic, or implied consent) if the patient could not give verbal or written consent.

headings.title: Short title of Simon's Law

headings.title: Definitions of end-of-life decision order and medical judgment
headings.reviewNote: Defines end-of-life medical decision order and reasonable medical judgment for life-sustaining treatment determinations.

headings.title: Mandatory parental consent for minor DNR orders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits instituting a DNR or similar physician order for a non-ward unemancipated minor without written or oral consent (with two witnesses if oral) of at least one parent or legal guardian, recorded immediately in the medical record.

headings.title: Forty-eight-hour diligent contact effort exception
headings.reviewNote: Exempts subsection 3 consent requirements if a reasonably diligent effort of at least 48 hours without success has been made to contact and inform each known parent or legal guardian.

headings.title: Oral or written revocation of DNR consent by parent
headings.reviewNote: Allows a parent or guardian to revoke prior DNR consent orally or in writing at any time.

headings.title: Juvenile court end-of-life orders and parental revocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes juvenile or family courts to issue end-of-life decision orders or appoint a guardian (excluding the children's division) for children under section 211.031 jurisdiction, and permits oral or written parental revocation upon return of custody (source note flags plural forms in original rolls of H.B. 138, 2019).

headings.title: Authority of consenting relative caregivers under section 431.058

headings.title: Preservation of medical futility determinations and pain relief
headings.reviewNote: Provides that section does not mandate treatments judged medically futile, harmful, or causing unnecessary pain.

headings.title: Cessation of CPR when clinical recovery is unachievable
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that providers are not required to continue resuscitation when, in reasonable medical judgment, no benefit or recovery is possible.

headings.title: Distribution of pilot program grants upon appropriation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department upon appropriation to award pilot grants to qualified clinical providers.

headings.title: Three-year departmental evaluation and outcome report
headings.reviewNote: Requires an evaluation and clinical report to the general assembly three years after initial grant administration.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for pilot program guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to promulgate rules establishing eligibility guidelines and implementing this section, subject to chapter 536 compliance and nonseverability after August 28, 2011.

headings.title: Short title of Adoption Awareness Law

headings.title: Department duty to educate the public regarding adoption

headings.title: Authorization of ongoing statewide adoption advertising campaign
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes establishing and operating an ongoing multimedia advertising campaign promoting domestic adoption.

headings.title: Contingency on legislative appropriations for awareness activities
headings.reviewNote: Provides that public education and advertising campaigns are subject to available legislative appropriations.

headings.title: Mandatory chapter 536 rulemaking by social services

headings.title: Director authority to monitor and recommend AHEC policy

headings.title: Program duties and healthcare recruitment initiatives

headings.title: Biennial reporting to general assembly on diabetes metrics
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting a biennial report to the general assembly assessing diabetes prevalence, medical costs, and program impacts.
